To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best balance of Type 1 error and statistical power for testing intervening variable effects is the test of joint significance of the 2 effects comprising the effect.

the best method to test an intervening variable effect is to use the difference-in-coefficient test, and that the best method for testing a set of intervening variable effects is to use the test of the set.

the best method to test for the statistical significance of an intervening variable effect is to test the joint significance of two effects, one from each of the two causal pathways, that comprise that effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what the best way is to test for mediation in a causal analysis.
a method of determining whether the effect of a variable on a dependent variable is mediated by a second intervening variable.
the problem of the intervening variable in the causal analysis of the effects of one variable on another.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the test of the intervening variable is best done with the test of the significance of the two coefficients, but the 4 methods that are based on the product of the coefficients are the best methods for most purposes.
the Baron and Kenny method is a poor test of the significance of the intervening-variable effect and that the best method is the joint test of the effects comprising the intervening-variable effect.
the best method is the test of joint significance of the effects comprising the intervening variables effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most accurate Type 1 error rates and the greatest statistical power are found with the 3 methods that use the distribution of the intervening variable product: (a) the test of the product, (b) the difference between the indirect and direct effect (the difference-in-coefficiencies method), and (c) the test of a regression equation with the intervening variable as the independent variable.

the most accurate Type 1 error rate and statistical power are found in the test of the two effects that comprise the intervening variable effect, the test of the product, and the test of the differences between coefficients.
the most appropriate method depends on the type of intervening variable effect and the sample size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most common method to test the intervening variable effect has poor statistical power and should not be used.
there are many methods to test intervening variable effects, but only 2 or 3 are recommended.

the methods that have the best Type I error rates, statistical power, and balance of Type I errors and power across all cases are not the most commonly used methods. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
